items.markdown:
![What is information architecture & why does it matter?](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/10081734-2633-0066-0000-29f1b46b05d7:4)
Information architecture (IA) is `the structural design, organization, and labeling of digital products like websites and apps to make content easy to find and use`.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_architecture)[[2]](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/blogs/information-architecture/)

### Key Components of IA

- **Organization Systems:** How content is grouped, such as hierarchical (broad to specific), sequential (step-by-step), or matrix (user-selectable) paths.
- **Labeling Systems:** The names and terms used for categories, menus, and buttons so users instantly know what they mean.
- **Navigation Systems:** The paths and tools (like menus or breadcrumbs) that help users move through a system.
- **Search Systems:** The search bar and filters that help users find specific items directly.[[1]](https://www.coursera.org/articles/information-architecture)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_architecture)

### Core Principles

- **Objects:** Treat content as living things with unique structures and lifecycles (like articles, images, or products).
- **Choices:** Keep user options focused and clear to avoid decision fatigue.
- **Disclosure:** Show information progressively in layers so users are not overloaded.
- **Exemplars:** Use clear examples to explain abstract categories.[[1]](https://webfirst.uark.edu/site-toolkit/information-architecture.php)

### Common Research Methods

- [Card Sorting](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ia-study-guide/) : A user-research method where participants group content topics to reveal mental models.
- **Tree Testing:** A method to test if users can easily find specific items within a proposed [Information Architecture: A Complete Guide For Beginners](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/blogs/information-architecture/) structure.[[1]](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ia-study-guide/)[[2]](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/blogs/information-architecture/)

If you're working on a project, tell me:

- **What type of product** are you designing (e.g., e-commerce site, mobile app, blog)?
- **What is the main goal** for your users?

I can help you outline an initial category hierarchy or suggest how to organize your navigation.
